title: SPHMC restricted-Gaussian fiber Wasserstein contraction
source_anchor: arXiv:2609.06906v1 Lemma 4.17; Lee-Shen-Tian arXiv:2010.03106v4 Lemma 2 proof, PDF pp.16-17, equations (10)-(11)
target_statement: For alpha>0 and eta>0, prove that the normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers R_eta,y(dx) proportional to exp(-V(x)-||x-y||^2/(2 eta)) dx of an alpha-strongly convex potential satisfy W2(R_eta,y,R_eta,y') <= ||y-y'||/(1+alpha eta); then specialize alpha=kappa^{-1} to the exact kappa/(kappa+eta) factor in SPHMC Lemma 4.17.

Samplinglib CommonNoiseContraction and Wasserstein coupling infrastructure

Lee-Shen-Tian arXiv:2010.03106v4 Lemma 2 and Chen-Chewi-Salim-Wibisono arXiv:2202.06386 Appendix A.2
new_shared_declarations: planned: a finite-dimensional strong-convex Gibbs LSI/T2 theorem with canonical KL and Fisher semantics
reuse_plan.decision_reason: Recovery already has a stronger compiled disintegration theorem. The missing mathematical edge is the analytic W2 contraction itself, shared with the textbook proximal-sampler route. Assuming T2 or the desired coupling cost in a route-local wrapper would merely restate the missing conclusion.

graph_contribution.visual_review: Not applicable before a compiled declaration exists; this blocker must not be rendered blue.

conceptual_mirror_audit.reason: The paper proof is the standard LSI-T2-relative-Fisher route. No new categorical or cross-domain equivalence is asserted.

focused_checks: Read-only Samplinglib and pinned-Mathlib API search found no Talagrand T2, strong-convex Gibbs LSI instance, posterior-tilt W2 stability, Caffarelli contraction or Wasserstein resolvent theorem.
Independent API audit confirmed that RGO recovery already compiles in Tests/GaussianConditionalKernel.lean and RGOBackward.rgo_backward_recovery, so no recovery wrapper is admissible.
Independent source audit reconstructed the exact Lee-Shen-Tian coefficient chain and rejected the larger JKO route for this SAU.
evidence.proof_review: Two independent read-only audits agree that the absent edge is analytic fiberwise W2 contraction, not kernel recovery or coefficient algebra. A later independent pair accepted the canonical LSI-to-finite-KL/Fisher prerequisite without promoting the Gibbs LSI/T2 hub.
evidence.independent_verification: ASTIS-RT-20261003-CanonicalLogSobolev verifies the conditional canonical bridge only.
evidence.source_review: Lee-Shen-Tian Lemma 2 uses curvature lambda=alpha+eta^{-1}, Talagrand W2^2<=2 KL/lambda, LSI KL<=FI/(2 lambda), and the exact constant relative score (y-y')/eta, yielding (1+alpha eta)^{-2} after squaring.
evidence.execution_boundary: No W2 theorem is claimed. Recovery, center-law contraction, SPHMC Theorem 1.1, all-q initialization, Picard dynamics and query cost remain separate.

blocked.reason: missing-formal-library-analytic-backend: the exact normalized quadratic relative-score representative and its explicit relative-Fisher energy now compile, with common normalizer base and left integration law separated. Neither Samplinglib nor pinned Mathlib yet supplies the finite-dimensional strong-convex Gibbs log-Sobolev/Talagrand transport theorem or the score-domain adapter needed to insert this value into that backend. The alternative JKO proof needs an even larger absent Wasserstein subdifferential and displacement-convexity substrate.

source_detail_audit.primary_anchor: Lemma 4.17, with cited proof expanded by arXiv:2010.03106v4 Lemma 2, PDF pp.16-17, equations (10)-(11)
source_detail_audit.gap: SPHMC calls invariance and contraction standard and cites prior work; it does not state the normalization, P2, absolute-continuity, relative-score or transport-inequality obligations needed by Lean.

consulted.hypothesis_adapter: Set alpha=kappa^{-1}; the quadratic tilt adds eta^{-1} curvature, and the relative score is the constant vector (y-y')/eta.

Confirms the same factor through Wasserstein proximal-point strong monotonicity; this route is retained as source corroboration but retired for implementation because its formal substrate is strictly larger.

source_detail_audit.fidelity_boundary: The upper Hessian bound in SPHMC Lemma 4.17 is not used for this fiber contraction. No contraction follows from smoothness alone, and no assumed coupling may encode the desired cost.
